sentences.text: Dzharaonyx was a relatively small dinosaur belonging to the group of alvarezsaurid theropods.
Subsequent researchers estimated this animal was about 50 cm long and weighed approximately 1.75 kg.
The species is distinguished by unique anatomical features, including opisthocoelous dorsal vertebrae, a large olecranon process, an arctometatarsus, and small flexor tubercles on its toe claws.
Scientists know the animal from a series of well-preserved but dissociated postcranial material.
The shape of the humerus in Dzharaonyx is intermediate between that of Patagonykus and Mononykus.
Dzharaonyx holds the distinction of being the oldest known Parvicursorinae to date.
The specific epithet "eski" means "old" in the Uzbek language, reflecting this ancient status.
All remains of Dzharaonyx were found at the Dzharakuduk locality in the Kyzylkum Desert of Uzbekistan within the Upper Cretaceous Bissekty Formation.
Lev Nesov discovered the first alvarezsaurid remains that would later be classified as Dzharaonyx between 1977 and 1994.
Additional remains were discovered between 1997 and 2006 by the URBAC joint-paleontological expedition.
Dzharaonyx was formally named and described in 2022 by Alexander Averianov and Hans Dieter-Sues.
By 2017, only seven bones confidently identified as alvarezsaurs had been found among over 3,500 catalogued dinosaur fossils.
Researchers suggest Dzharaonyx may have specialized in feeding on colonial insects like ants due to its hand morphology and the spread of angiosperms.
The Dzharakuduk locality also yielded fossils of Timurlengia, Bissektipelta, Ulughbegsaurus, enantiornithines, and amphibians.
Dzharaonyx belongs to the family Alvarezsauridae.
Phylogenetic analysis places Dzharaonyx within the monophyletic subfamily Parvicursorinae.
Dzharaonyx represents the oldest known record of Parvicursorinae, suggesting an Asian origin for the group.
Phylogenetic analysis places Dzharaonyx in a polytomy with other Asian members of Parvicursorinae.
Dzharaonyx lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 93 to 89 million years ago in the Turonian stage, with a specific time range from 93.9 to 89.8 million years ago.
Dzharaonyx lived in what is now Asia.
Geological evidence indicates that a braided river system replaced the coastline in the environment where Dzharaonyx lived.
The Bissekty Formation where Dzharaonyx fossils were found represents a brackish environment.
